entities.summary:
The Master and Margarita is a novel by Mikhail Bulgakov, written in the late 1920s and first published in 1966. Set in Soviet Moscow, the novel explores the intersection of reality and fantasy through the story of the Devil's visit to the city. The Master and Margarita is a masterpiece of 20th-century literature, weaving together elements of surrealism, philosophy, and mysticism. Its exploration of the human condition, morality, and the nature of reality continues to captivate readers today.

The novel's complex narrative is structured around the Master's struggle with his wife, Margarita, and his own identity, as well as the Devil's schemes to wreak havoc on the city. Through its use of magical realism and vivid characterization, The Master and Margarita offers a profound commentary on the nature of reality and the human experience.

The novel's influence can be seen in the works of many later authors, including Philip Roth and Don DeLillo. Its exploration of the human condition continues to resonate with readers today, making it a timeless classic of 20th-century literature.

The Master and Margarita has been recognized as one of the greatest novels of the 20th century, and its influence can be seen in many aspects of modern culture, from film and literature to music and art. Its exploration of the human condition and the nature of reality continues to captivate readers today, making it a work of enduring significance.

This novel is a must-read for anyone interested in 20th-century literature, surrealism, philosophy, or the human condition. Its exploration of the nature of reality and the human experience continues to resonate with readers today, making it a work of enduring significance.
